title: Harden the producer egress probe and test its checks on real transcripts
description:
## Context

Tracer 2 slice T2 (`docs/notes/tracer-2.md`) proves the runner producer's sandbox with an egress probe (`producer.yml` with `egress_probe=true`). On 2026-11-07 four probe runs were needed. Two of the failures were in the probe itself, not in the producer (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L6 to L8 and L11):

- Run 42405543342: the model added the Bash tool's `allowed_domains` parameter to its first `curl`. That attempt was refused, and the prompt's "do not retry" line stopped it before the plain `curl` that shows the sandbox proxy's 403. The check printed `BOUNDARY CHECK INVALID: egress probe got no 403`.
- The egress check once read only the first `curl` attempt. Replaying run 42400602621's real transcript found that bug before it landed.
- A workflow step used `mapfile`, a bash 4 builtin. The tests run steps with the first `bash` on `PATH`, which is 3.2 on macOS, so the owner's preflight failed.

Without this, every change to a producer check risks another failed probe and another signed landing.

## Outcome

A probe run on an unchanged producer prints `BOUNDARY HELD: unlisted command denied` and `BOUNDARY HELD: egress to example.com`, and every producer check step is tested against real probe transcripts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The probe prompt in `scripts/ci/producer.ts` tells the agent not to set the Bash tool's `allowed_domains` parameter. Checked by a test on `agentPrompt(…, true)`.
- [ ] The transcripts of runs 42389828816, 42400602621, 42403610421 and 42405543342 are stored under `test/fixtures/producer/`, and vitest runs the permission-mode, unlisted-command and egress steps against each, asserting the line each should print. Checked by `npm run check:test`.
- [ ] A test fails when a `run:` block in any workflow uses `mapfile`, `readarray`, `declare -A` or `${x,,}`. Checked by adding one and seeing the test fail.
- [ ] One owner-dispatched probe prints both `BOUNDARY HELD` lines. Checked by reading the agent job's log.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the probe tests. The unlisted command stays a write (`touch probe-unlisted`), because Claude Code runs its read-only commands without approval in every mode.

## Open questions

- Should the transcripts be trimmed of model text before they are committed? They hold no credentials, but they hold the runner's kernel string and file paths.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R87 (the prompt). Protected files, so this is a signed batch under `proposals/`.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/1 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Decide how a producer delivery gets checks that main's ruleset counts
description:
## Context

The `protect main` ruleset requires the status check `checks` from the GitHub Actions app (integration ID 15368). On 2026-11-07 the runner producer's first delivery, commit `8147bc5` on `candidate/TASK-T2-GOOD-1`, was refused by `main` with `GH013: Required status check "checks" is expected`. Its `checks` had passed in a `pipeline.yml` run started by the producer's dispatch job (`workflow_dispatch` by `github-actions[bot]`, run 42406055336): same name, same app ID, same commit. The owner then pushed the same commit to `candidate/t2-good-1-owner`; that `push` run's `checks` (run 42406663498) was counted and `main` accepted the commit.

So SPEC-001-R209's premise, that the dispatch makes a producer delivery landable, does not hold. Until this is decided, every producer delivery needs the owner to re-push it. `docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L3.

## Outcome

A recorded owner decision, and the producer changed to match, so that a producer delivery reaches a state `main` accepts with the fewest owner actions the threat model allows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An experiment separates event from actor: the owner runs `gh workflow run pipeline.yml --ref candidate/<branch>` on a producer branch, then tries to push that commit to `main`. Result recorded in `docs/verification.md`.
- [ ] The options are compared in a decision note: (a) the owner re-pushes each delivery, as decision 0004 Phase A already says; (b) the owner dispatches `pipeline.yml`; (c) a GitHub App token for the publish job, which adds a key holder; (d) decision 0004 Phase B's promote App.
- [ ] SPEC-001-R209 is amended or withdrawn to match, with a test naming it. Checked by the trace check.
- [ ] One producer delivery lands under the chosen option. Checked by `main`'s run.

## Out of scope

- Building the promote App itself (0004 Phase B).

## Open questions

- Is the refusal about the `workflow_dispatch` event or about the `GITHUB_TOKEN` actor? The experiment above answers it.
- Does GitHub document this behaviour for rulesets? Not found on 2026-11-07.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R209. Part of Tracer 2 slice T3.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/2 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Update 2026-11-07: the docs answer the experiment

GitHub documents the rule, so the experiment in the first acceptance criterion is no longer needed to separate event from actor. "Troubleshooting required status checks" says checks from workflow jobs count only when the run was started by `push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_target`, `deployment` or `deployment_status`, and that checks from a `workflow_dispatch` run "do not satisfy a required status check in a branch ruleset" even when they pass. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks, read 2026-11-07, recorded in `docs/verification.md`.

Consequences:

- Option (b), the owner dispatching `pipeline.yml`, cannot work: it is still a `workflow_dispatch` run.
- The open question "event or actor?" is answered: the event. Observed only for the bot's run (42406055336); an owner-dispatched run is predicted to fail the same way and was not run.
- The first acceptance criterion is replaced by the citation. If observed proof is wanted, the next producer delivery can carry it at the cost of one `gh workflow run` and one refused push.
- Still to decide among (a) the owner re-pushes, which `producer.sh` (`who-gets-the-keys-j4e`) can reduce to one command; (c) a GitHub App token for the publish job, whose push starts a `push` run but adds a key holder and a secret, against SPEC-001-R85; (d) the promote App; and (e), found in the same docs, a pull request.
- (e): a pull request the publish job opens with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts `pull_request` runs "in an approval-required state", and "a user with write access to the repository can start the runs by selecting Approve workflows to run" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token, read 2026-11-07). `pull_request` is an eligible event, so one owner click could replace the re-push with no new key holder. Not tested, and three things stand in the way: `pipeline.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger; such a run checks out GitHub's test merge commit under `refs/pull/<n>/merge`, which has no `Spec:` trailer for the trace check and a ref the receipt pin refuses (SPEC-001-R50), so the workflow would have to check out the head commit; and it is not yet confirmed that its check runs attach to the head commit.
- SPEC-001-R209's dispatch job still gives an early, uncounted signal that a delivery passes. Its premise, that it makes a delivery landable, is wrong.

## Decision 2026-11-07

The owner chose (a), with SPEC-001-R209 withdrawn. `land.sh --delivery candidate/<task>` re-pushes the delivery to `candidate/<task>-owner` and moves `main` (new SPEC-001-R210). Staged in `proposals/t3-delivery-landing/`; the comparison and owner steps are in `docs/notes/tracer-2-t3-landing.md`. Done when that batch has landed and one producer delivery has landed with `--delivery`, the last acceptance criterion. Option (e) stays open as a later experiment.

## Correction 2026-11-08

The decision above says SPEC-001-R209 withdrawn. As staged now, R209 is amended instead, to forbid the dispatch: the first signed landing, `e5ed597`, failed the trace check because the signed commit `4812f27` names R209 in its `Spec:` trailer. The effect on the workflows is the same.

## Update 2026-11-08: landed

The batch landed as `c708a0e`: R209 amended (the producer starts no workflow run), R40 push-only, R210 `land.sh --delivery`. Still open: the last acceptance criterion, one producer delivery landed with `land.sh --delivery`. T4 is the planned first one.

## Closed 2026-11-08

The first producer delivery landed through `scripts/bootstrap/land.sh --delivery`: `9f959a3` for TASK-T4-DUP-COLUMNS, with `candidate/TASK-T4-DUP-COLUMNS-owner` run 113 reporting the checks `main` counts, then `main` run 114 and its deploy.

title: Make land.sh test a batch before signing and explain a cancelled deploy
description:
## Context

`scripts/bootstrap/land.sh` moves a staged batch under `proposals/` into place, asks the owner to sign, runs the candidate checks, pushes to `main` and watches the deploy. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L10 and L13):

- Before each of four signed landings, the owner pasted a one-line "preflight" that ran `tsc`, ESLint and vitest on the moved files. It broke three times: zsh's read-only `status` variable, macOS bash 3.2 lacking `mapfile`, and a terminal whose Node was 24.1 while `package.json` needs 24.11 or later.
- When a newer push cancelled the pending deploy, `land.sh` printed "main's run did not pass ... fix the problem in a new commit on top", although there was nothing to fix. This was already in the backlog of `docs/notes/carry-over-2026-11-07.md`.

## Outcome

`land.sh` runs the batch's tests itself before it asks for a signature, and tells the owner accurately what happened to `main`'s run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before the signing prompt, `land.sh` checks Node against `package.json` engines, runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint on the moved TypeScript and vitest on the moved tests, in a temporary worktree, and refuses to sign if any fails. Checked by `test/land.test.ts` with a stub `npm` and `npx`.
- [ ] It runs under `bash` whatever the owner's shell is. Checked by `bash -n` and the existing tests.
- [ ] When `main`'s run failed only because the deploy was cancelled or rejected, it names that job and says nothing needs fixing. Checked by a test with a stubbed `gh run view`.
- [ ] The README's "How changes land" and the batch notes drop the separate preflight step.

## Out of scope

- Running the slow checks (`sast`, `sca`, `mutation`) locally; the candidate run covers them.

## Open questions

- Should it run the whole `npm run checks` before signing? It stops at `signatures` for an unsigned protected change, so only the checks before it would run.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R41 covers `land.sh` today; a new requirement may be clearer. Protected file, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/3 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Update 2026-11-08

The pre-sign run must include `node scripts/checks.ts trace` on the moved tree, not only tsc, ESLint and vitest. A preflight without it let `e5ed597` be signed although removing SPEC-001-R209 failed trace (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L19).

## Update 2026-11-08: say where to approve

While `main`'s deploy waits, `land.sh` shows only `* deploy to sandbox`. It prints `gh run view <id> --web` once, before `gh run watch` starts, and the watch redraws the screen every 3 seconds, so the pointer scrolls away. On 2026-11-08 the owner had to ask for the run's URL at every landing.

- [ ] When the deploy job starts waiting, `land.sh` prints one line with the run's URL, `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>`, and says to approve the `sandbox` deployment there. It prints the same line again after the watch ends. Checked by a test with a stub `gh` that reports the deploy job as `waiting`.
- [ ] Before signing, `land.sh` runs `git apply --check` in the moved tree for every scenario patch that touches a file the batch changes, and refuses to sign if one fails. T3a broke B18 this way (lesson L20). Checked by a test with a batch that changes a patched file.

title: Add producer.sh to dispatch, find and summarise producer runs
description:
## Context

The owner starts the runner producer (`.github/workflows/producer.yml`) with `gh workflow run`, then has to find the new run and read its result. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L14):

- `sleep 5 && gh run list --limit 1` twice returned the previous run, because the new one was not listed yet.
- Reading a result meant `gh run view --log` piped through `grep`, and the log also prints each step's script text, which holds the same `BOUNDARY` words.
- It was unclear when `main` had moved far enough for a dispatch to run the newly landed `producer.yml`.

## Outcome

One command per use: `scripts/bootstrap/producer.sh probe` and `scripts/bootstrap/producer.sh task <ID> [--spec <ID>] --subject <text> --prompt <text>`. Each dispatches, finds the run created after its own dispatch time, watches it, and prints only the result lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] It refuses to dispatch unless the local `main` equals `origin/main`, and prints the SHA it dispatches on. Checked by a test with a stub `git`.
- [ ] It identifies the new run by `createdAt` after the dispatch time and `headSha`, never by `--limit 1` alone. Checked by a test with a stub `gh` that lists an older run first.
- [ ] It prints only the `Permission mode:`, `BOUNDARY`, `RUN ENDED` and `CHECK` lines from the agent job, and for a task also the candidate branch and its `pipeline.yml` run's conclusion. Checked by a test on a recorded log.
- [ ] It exits non-zero on any `BROKEN`, `INVALID` or `CHECK … FAILED` line.

## Out of scope

- Landing the delivery on `main`; see `who-gets-the-keys-nlq`.

## Open questions

- None.

Spec impact: none required; a test names an existing producer requirement. Protected path (`scripts/bootstrap/`), so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/4 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Update 2026-11-07

Landing is no longer out of scope elsewhere: `scripts/bootstrap/land.sh --delivery candidate/<task>` (SPEC-001-R210, staged in `proposals/t3-delivery-landing/`) lands a delivery. `producer.sh task` can end by printing that command, as the publish job now does.

title: Run the deploy job only when deployable paths change
description:
## Context

Every push to `main` runs `pipeline.yml`'s deploy job, which waits for the `sandbox` reviewer, a gate. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L12) docs-only and `proposals/`-only commits produced deploys with nothing to deploy. Because a deploy waiting for approval holds the `pipeline-deploy` concurrency slot:

- run 65's stale deploy blocked the deploy of `main`'s tip until the owner rejected it;
- one approval went to a stale run, refused by the deploy-tip check (SPEC-001-R190);
- one of the owner's pending deploys was cancelled when a newer run queued.

Each of these cost the owner a round of confusion and an extra approval.

## Outcome

Commits that change nothing deployable never wait at the deploy gate, and the receipt still records every commit on `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The deploy job runs only when the pushed range touches a deployable path: `src/`, `infra/sandbox/`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or the build steps of `pipeline.yml`. Otherwise it is skipped with a line naming why. Checked by a workflow test.
- [ ] A commit range that touches only `docs/` or `proposals/` plans no deploy. Checked by a `main` run after landing.
- [ ] Deploy-tip (SPEC-001-R190) still refuses any deploy that is not `main`'s tip. Checked by the existing tests.
- [ ] Decision note: whether a skipped deploy weakens the receipt or the "only main's tip deploys" story.

## Out of scope

- Removing the `sandbox` gate (decision 0004 Phase C, deploy by tier).

## Open questions

- Should the path list live in `specs/` as policy, so that widening it needs a signature?
- Does skipping the deploy for an infra-free commit leave drift undetected? Terraform plans no change today in that case.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R40 (amend). Protected files, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/5 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Make aws-setup.sh refuse a Bedrock model the account cannot call
description:
## Context

`scripts/bootstrap/aws-setup.sh` checks only that the chosen `us.anthropic.` inference profile is `ACTIVE`. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L1) that was not enough in the sandbox account:

- Sonnet 5.5's profile was `ACTIVE`, but `get-foundation-model-availability` showed `agreementAvailability: NOT_AVAILABLE` for every Claude model, since none had ever been accepted.
- After the owner accepted the Marketplace agreement (`create-foundation-model-agreement`; `AVAILABLE` within 30 seconds), calls still failed with `AccessDeniedException ... is not available for this account`. Service Quotas showed the account's applied cross-region quota as 0 tokens per minute for every Claude 4.7 and 5.x model, against a default of 6,000,000.
- The producer was moved to Sonnet 4.6, which has 6,000,000. A quota increase for Sonnet 5.5 (quota `L-94A31E46`, requested 7,000,000) is pending with a request whose ID is in the sandbox account's Service Quotas console.

A setup that passed its checks left both the producer and triage unable to call their model.

## Outcome

`aws-setup.sh` refuses, before any write, a model the account cannot call, and says which layer is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For `TRIAGE_MODEL` and `producer_inference_profile`, it checks `agreementAvailability` is `AVAILABLE`, `authorizationStatus` is `AUTHORIZED`, and the applied cross-region quota is above 0, then makes one `converse` call with the sandbox admin profile. On failure it prints which of the four failed and changes nothing. Checked by `test/aws-setup.test.ts` with stub `aws` responses for each case.
- [ ] `docs/verification.md` cites the AWS docs for each call it relies on, with dates.
- [ ] When the Sonnet 5.5 request is approved: decide whether to move back, and record the decision.

## Out of scope

- Accepting agreements automatically; the owner accepts them, because they are Marketplace commitments.

## Open questions

- Does the quota check need to cover every Region a `us.` profile routes to? On 2026-11-07, agreement status was the same in us-east-1, us-east-2 and us-west-2.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R28 and R30 (aws-setup tests). Protected path, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/6 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Make the break-glass role assumable with MFA, and drill it
description:
## Context

`who-gets-the-keys-break-glass` (`infra/sandbox/iam.tf`) is the only role the SCP in `infra/org` lets change the workload's roles, its own trust policy included. Its trust requires `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent`. On 2026-11-07 the owner could not assume it from IAM Identity Center through `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` (`AccessDenied` on `sts:AssumeRole`). Inference: the chained session does not carry the MFA flag. The role had never been assumed. To change the producer's model, the owner instead detached the SCP from the management account for one `aws-setup.sh` run, which re-attached it (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L2; `docs/verification.md`, "Break-glass from IAM Identity Center").

A break-glass role nobody can assume fails exactly when it is needed.

## Outcome

The owner can assume break-glass with MFA from their own machine, the alert email arrives, and a scheduled drill proves it still works.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Research, with dated AWS doc citations: whether `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` is present for Identity Center sessions, for role chains from them, and for an IAM user using `--serial-number` and `--token-code`.
- [ ] A Terraform-managed principal whose only permission is `sts:AssumeRole` on break-glass, with an MFA device the owner registers by hand, and the SCP updated so only break-glass can change it. Checked by `node scripts/checks.ts iac` and a plan review.
- [ ] README "AWS setup" gives the owner the profile and a first `aws sts get-caller-identity` through break-glass. Checked by the owner seeing the role ARN and the alert email.
- [ ] A drill, a quarterly reminder or scheduled check, repeats that call. Checked by the first drill.

## Out of scope

- Using break-glass for routine changes; the pipeline stays the normal path.

## Open questions

- Does the owner's YubiKey OATH-TOTP applet work for AWS CLI MFA?
- Is a long-lived access key, useless without MFA, acceptable under the talk's "who gets the keys" thesis, or should the principal be console-only?

Spec impact: a new SPEC-001 requirement. Protected paths, so a signed batch. A suggested-task card for this exists in the Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/7 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Version the cloud session setup script in the repo
description:
## Context

Claude Code cloud sessions for this repository run in a claude.ai cloud environment whose setup script lives in claude.ai, not in the repo. On 2026-11-07 it was recorded in the README ("Cloud session environment"): Node v24.22.2 checked against nodejs.org's SHA-256, the pinned check CLIs, and `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. A fresh session confirmed every version and a passing typecheck. Nothing detects drift between the README copy and claude.ai. The owner decided to fold the versioned script into Tracer 2 slice T3 (`docs/notes/tracer-2.md`, owner decisions; `docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L4).

## Outcome

The setup script lives in the repo, under a requirement, and claude.ai holds only a one-line call to it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/bootstrap/cloud-session-setup.sh` holds the README's script, run from the repository root. Checked by `bash -n` and a test that the Node SHA-256 in it matches `docs/verification.md`.
- [ ] A new SPEC-001 requirement names it, with a test naming the requirement. Checked by the trace check.
- [ ] The claude.ai setup script becomes `if [ -d who-gets-the-keys ]; then bash who-gets-the-keys/scripts/bootstrap/cloud-session-setup.sh; fi`, set by the owner. Checked by a fresh session printing `node v24.22.2` and passing `npm run check:typecheck`.
- [ ] The README section points at the script instead of copying it.

## Out of scope

- Network policy for the environment; it stays "Full" until someone tests a limited allowlist.

## Open questions

- The script runs as root from whatever branch the session checks out. Is that acceptable for sessions on agent-written branches? Inference: yes, because it only affects that session's own container.

Spec impact: a new SPEC-001 requirement. Protected path, so part of T3's signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/8 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Closed 2026-11-11

`proposals/cloud-session-setup/` landed on 2026-11-09 as the owner-signed `759a28f` (SPEC-001-R211), main run 42540430148. The owner then made the claude.ai environment `who-gets-the-keys` with the README's one-line setup script, and the first session in it printed `node --version` v24.22.2 and passed `npm run check:typecheck`. The claims ledger's C04 no longer cites this item.

title: Add the agent's owner-step rules to CLAUDE.md
description:
## Context

On 2026-11-07 the agent walked the owner through Tracer 2 slices T1 and T2. Several delays came from the agent's own instructions, not from the system (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L15 to L18):

- "Wait for the run" did not say which run or which terminal.
- Next steps were sent while a previous one was still running.
- The agent pushed staging commits to `main` while one of the owner's deploys waited for approval, which stranded one deploy and cancelled another.
- Probes were designed before checking the platform's documented behaviour. `uname` was used as an "unlisted" command, though Claude Code runs it without approval in every mode.

`CLAUDE.md` is the agent's persistent instruction file and a protected path.

## Outcome

`CLAUDE.md` has an "Owner steps" section the agent follows in every session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every owner step names the terminal, the exact command, the one line that means success, and what to do on anything else.
- [ ] One step at a time: the agent reads the previous step's result itself before giving the next.
- [ ] The agent never pushes to `main` while any `main` deploy waits for approval, and checks with the Actions API before each push.
- [ ] Before a probe or check that relies on platform behaviour, the agent quotes the documentation it relies on, with the URL and date, and replays any recorded transcript through the check.
- [ ] Checked by approver review of the signed change. These rules are not machine-checkable.

## Out of scope

- Rules for the runner producer's prompt; those live in `scripts/ci/producer.ts`.

## Open questions

- None.

Spec impact: none. `CLAUDE.md` is protected, so it goes in T3's signed batch as `proposals/CLAUDE.proposed.md`.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/9 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Added 2026-11-08: never refer to a private repository

This repository is public. No file, commit message, branch name or PR text may name a private repository, link to it, or cite its paths, commit SHAs or release names. On 2026-11-08 an agent edit to `factory-video/README.md` left such a reference in place in the same file, and the owner caught it. Acceptance: the rule is in `CLAUDE.md` under "Conventions", and a check or commit hook refuses a commit whose diff or message adds a name on a denylist of the owner's private repositories, kept outside this repository. Checked by a test that commits such a line and sees it refused. Open question: where the denylist lives, since listing private names here would itself break the rule.

## Added 2026-11-08: no session link in commits

Owner decision D24 (`docs/deviations.md`) names no Claude Code session in this repository. Agent commits carry no `Claude-Session:` trailer; until 2026-11-08 they did, in 42 commits. Acceptance: the rule is in `CLAUDE.md`, and a commit hook refuses a message with `claude.ai/code/session_`, checked by a test.

title: Protect .npmrc and run the checks without npm's project config
description:
## Context

`.npmrc` is not in `specs/protected-paths.txt`. A project `.npmrc` with `node-options=--import=./docs/notes/x.mjs` makes every `npm run <script>` load that module first. `pipeline.yml`'s checks job runs `npm run checks`, and its build job runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` then `npm run build`. An unsigned commit pushed to `candidate/**` that adds `.npmrc` plus a module under an unprotected path could therefore make the checks exit 0, the `signatures` check included, and alter `dist/function.zip` before it is attested.

An independent review of the runner producer found this on 2026-11-07. It reproduced the exit-code override with npm 10.9.9. The producer's own publish job now refuses any path outside `src/`, `test/`, `docs/` and `traceability.md`, but any other candidate push still has the gap. Decision 0004's planned R109, running `signatures` with `main`'s check code, would not catch it while the checks run through `npm run` in the candidate tree.

## Outcome

A commit cannot change how the pipeline's checks or build start.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.npmrc` is added to `specs/protected-paths.txt`, along with any other file that can inject code at Node or npm start-up, each justified. Checked by the `signatures` check failing on an unsigned `.npmrc`.
- [ ] `pipeline.yml` starts the checks and the build so that a project `.npmrc` cannot add Node options, for example `node scripts/checks.ts` instead of `npm run checks`, or npm config overrides. Checked against npm's documented config precedence and a scenario.
- [ ] A new scenario patch adds `.npmrc` with a `node-options` payload and is stopped with a named failure line. Checked by `npm run scenarios`.
- [ ] `scenarios.yml` and `video.yml` reviewed for the same pattern.

## Out of scope

- `NODE_OPTIONS` from the runner environment, which a commit cannot set.

## Open questions

- Which npm config sources does an environment override neutralise, per npm's docs?

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R12 (the protected list) plus a new scenario requirement. Protected paths, so a signed batch. A suggested-task card for this exists in the Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/10 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Add the deploy-tip check to the README's check table
description:

title: Rename the ratchet check to mutation-floor
description:

title: Explain why Dependabot alerts on main while the sca check passes
description:

title: Show the signer an authority digest before land.sh asks to sign
description:
## Context

`scripts/bootstrap/land.sh` shows a signed batch as a diffstat and offers the full diff in a pager, then asks "Sign and land?". The batch `proposals/t3-delivery-landing/` was about 600 changed lines, most of them test code. Reading that line by line before every signature is not workable, so a signer skims and approves. A security-key touch then proves presence, not comprehension: it still stops an agent acting alone, but not a persuasive one. The owner raised this on 2026-11-08 while landing that batch.

## Outcome

Before the signing prompt, `land.sh` prints a short digest computed from the diff by code, not by a model, that answers the questions only the signer can answer, and accounts for every changed line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Requirements: every requirement ID added, removed or reworded, with a word diff per ID. Checked by a test with a fixture spec change.
- [ ] Workflows: every job that gains or loses a permission, trigger, secret, environment or runner, from the YAML parsed before and after. Checked by a test with a fixture workflow change.
- [ ] Trust lists: any change to `approvers.txt`, `specs/protected-paths.txt`, `allowed-deps.txt`, `.github/egress/*.json` or `specs/sca-exceptions.toml`, shown in full. Checked by a test.
- [ ] Outbound actions: new executed (not printed) `git push`, `gh api -X`, `curl`, `aws` and `terraform` lines in scripts and workflow steps. Checked by a test that a printed command string is not listed.
- [ ] Evidence: test titles added or removed, per requirement ID.
- [ ] Every other changed line is counted as unclassified, per file, and a large unclassified count is flagged. Checked by a test.
- [ ] The pager stays available, as today.

## Out of scope

- A model-written summary: the digest must be deterministic so the signer can trust what it leaves out.
- Reviewing in a GitHub pull request: a better reading surface, but it does not reduce volume and adds an approval surface GitHub does not tie to the approver key.

## Open questions

- What unclassified line count should be flagged?
- Should the digest also show the independent review findings and how each was resolved, from a file the batch carries?
- Does `land.sh` stay bash-only, or may it call `node scripts/checks.ts digest` for the YAML parsing? `land.sh` runs no Node today.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R41 covers `land.sh` today; a new SPEC-001 requirement is clearer. Protected path, so a signed batch.

title: Stop issue-triage from billing for runs that end without a label
description:
## Context

`.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml` runs Claude on Bedrock for every new issue. On 2026-11-07 the ten issues opened for the Tracer 2 lessons started ten runs: 8 failed and 2 were cancelled, and none applied a label. Run 42407186413 shows why: `claude-code-action` ran `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` with `maxTurns: 5` and a `--json-schema`, the result was `error_max_turns` after 6 turns, so it returned no structured output and the job failed. That run reported `total_cost_usd: 0.5631357`. The owner's AWS budget alert on 2026-11-08 showed USD 10.06 against a USD 10 budget, after a rise of more than USD 5 in a day. Inference: most of that rise is these runs, about USD 0.56 each. Not yet confirmed in Cost Explorer.

## Outcome

A triage run either labels the issue or stops before calling the model, and its cost is visible in the job log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The triage prompt and turn limit let one run return the schema's structured output for a plain issue. Checked by one owner-opened test issue that gets its label.
- [ ] A run that ends without structured output prints its `total_cost_usd` and one failure line, not a template error. Checked by a test on the job's steps.
- [ ] A daily cap: triage stops starting the model after N runs in a day. Checked by a test.

## Out of scope

- Turning triage off. The owner can disable the workflow with `gh workflow disable issue-triage.yml` meanwhile.

## Open questions

- What daily cap and turn limit should the owner set?
- Should agents open issues in this repository at all, now that the backlog lives in `.tasks/backlog.jsonl`?

Spec impact: a new SPEC-001 requirement for triage's budget. Protected path, so a signed batch.

title: Decide and build the full scope rule: every unexempt commit needs a signed task
description:
## Context

Tracer 2 slice T3a (`proposals/t3-task-file/`) stages a thin SPEC-001-R66: the scope check judges only commits that carry a `Task:` trailer. An independent review on 2026-11-08 ranked this its one medium finding (M1): a commit escapes the check by leaving the trailer off, or by naming a broader signed task. The publish job always adds the trailer, so runner deliveries are covered; commits made in a session are not. Decision 0004's full R66 makes every commit that is not approver-signed, not a proven tightening and not drafting-only (`docs/`, `proposals/`) carry exactly one `Task:` trailer. That rule would also stop agent maintenance commits to `factory-video/` and `.tasks/` unless the owner signs a task for each. It rests on 0004's owner question "Whether interactive sessions may still deliver code", rank 6 in `docs/notes/factory-video-gaps.md`.

## Outcome

An owner decision on the full rule, recorded in decision 0004, and R66 amended to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner's answer, with the date, in decision 0004.
- [ ] If the full rule is chosen: R66 amended, a scenario where an untasked commit to `src/` fails with `CHECK scope FAILED: missing Task trailer`, and the drafting list decided (whether `.tasks/` and `factory-video/` join `docs/` and `proposals/`). Checked by `npm run scenarios`.
- [ ] `factory-video/claims.json` C10 and C18 move this item to built. Checked by `node factory-video/verify.mjs --only claims`.

## Out of scope

- The promote App (0004 Phase B).

## Open questions

- Decide before or after T4? The T3a review and its author recommend after.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R66 (amend). Protected, so a signed batch.

title: Renew or fix the sca exceptions that expire on 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-30
description:
## Context

The sca check (SPEC-001-R10) runs OSV-Scanner over every committed lockfile and ignores only the advisories in `specs/sca-exceptions.toml` whose `ignoreUntil` has not passed. On 2026-11-08 that file holds 7 exceptions, and an OSV-Scanner run that day, without the file, still reported all 7. When an exception expires, the sca check fails with that advisory's ID on every push, candidate and `main` alike, with no code change. `main` then accepts no commit until the exception is renewed or the package is upgraded. Inference from the fail-fast order (SPEC-001-R1): every scenario whose expected check comes after sca (trace, ratchet, signatures, slides, test, mutation) also stops at sca, and so does the video build, which runs `npm run checks` (SPEC-002-R3).

| Expires | Advisory | Package | Lockfile | Why it is excepted, per the file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-22 | GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 | zod 3.25.76 | `package-lock.json` | Only `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` pulls it in, and every release through 0.0.81 needs zod 3 |
| 2026-11-22 | GHSA-84m7-p3x7-pcfv | mcp 1.29.0 | `scripts/ci/requirements.txt` | semgrep pins `mcp==1.29.0`; the sast check starts no MCP server |
| 2026-11-22 | GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h | opentelemetry-api 1.37.0 | `scripts/ci/requirements.txt` | semgrep requires `opentelemetry-api~=1.37.0`; semgrep scan serves no HTTP |
| 2026-11-30 | GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 | minimatch 10.2.6 | `package-lock.json` | eslint, @eslint/config-array, Stryker and typescript-eslint all require minimatch 10.x |
| 2026-11-30 | GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23, GHSA-rwrf-2pqf-9j8j, GHSA-5h93-6whr-6q8j | mcp 1.29.0 | `scripts/ci/requirements.txt` | semgrep pins `mcp==1.29.0`; semgrep scan runs no MCP client or server |

Dependabot does not read `specs/sca-exceptions.toml`, so it alerts on these while the sca check passes. That is the likely answer to `who-gets-the-keys-0v4`. It is not confirmed, because the alert list was not read on 2026-11-08.

## Outcome

Before 2026-11-22, each of the 3 exceptions that expire that day is fixed by an upgrade or renewed with a re-checked reason. Before 2026-11-30, the same holds for the other 4. The sca check never fails on `main` because an exception lapsed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each of the 7 advisories, the batch's notes say whether a fixed version is now reachable, citing the registry page and the date checked. The pages to check are: a semgrep release on PyPI that drops `mcp==1.29.0` and `opentelemetry-api~=1.37.0`; an `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` release on npm after 0.0.81 that allows zod 4; and whether eslint, Stryker and typescript-eslint accept minimatch 11. Checked by reading the notes.
- [ ] Each advisory with a reachable fix is upgraded, and its exception is removed. Checked by `osv-scanner` reporting no such advisory over the changed lockfile, run without `--config`.
- [ ] Each remaining exception has a new `ignoreUntil` and a reason re-checked against the current advisory text. Checked by reading `specs/sca-exceptions.toml` in the signed commit.
- [ ] The batch lands on `main` before 2026-11-22. Checked by the landing commit's date and its candidate run's sca step passing.

## Out of scope

- Why Dependabot and the sca check disagree, which is `who-gets-the-keys-0v4`.
- Scanning `.github/workflows/` actions or `infra/*/.terraform.lock.hcl`, which the sca check does not read today.

## Open questions

- Renew for another 30 days, or upgrade where a fix exists even if it means a major version?
- Should the sca check warn, without failing, when an exception expires within 7 days? That would be a new SPEC-001 requirement.

Not verified on 2026-11-08: whether any newer semgrep, sandbox-runtime or tooling release already fixes these pins.

Spec impact: none for a renewal or an upgrade. `specs/sca-exceptions.toml`, `package-lock.json`, `package.json` and `scripts/ci/` are protected paths, so either path is an approver-signed batch.

title: Build an as-built factory video from evidence-based claim status
description:
## Context

The factory video shows the target state. `factory-video/claims.json` tags each on-screen claim built, partly built, planned, open or illustrative, but counts a claim as built when its requirement ID is in `specs/`. That means signed, not implemented: SPEC-014-R7 was signed on `main` at `c7c6b4d` with only expected-fail tests while the Lambda still returned 200 for a repeated column. The owner's answers of 2026-11-08 are in decision 0008, "Owner decisions, 2026-11-08".

## Outcome

A second video, as built at a named commit, rendered from the same scene and ledger, beside the unchanged target video.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The claims check computes status from evidence: built when the requirement is signed, a passing test names it (`it.fails` does not count) and, for a claim about a control, its scenario held in `scenarios.yml` on that commit; partly built when some cited IDs qualify. Checked by a test where a signed requirement with only `it.fails` tests is not built.
- [ ] The as-built render greys planned and open parts, outlines partly built ones with a "partly" tag, and stamps the short SHA and the count of built claims. Checked by `verify.mjs` on every frame.
- [ ] Unbuilt narration lines are muted, their captions kept with a "Planned:" prefix, and no voice is re-rendered. Checked by `verify.mjs`.
- [ ] A built claim that loses its evidence fails the claims job on `main` without blocking it. Checked by a test.
- [ ] The as-built video is rendered only when a claim's status changes. Checked by the workflow's decision step.

## Out of scope

- Changing the target video or the deck, which keeps the target only.
- Making the claims job a check of record; the owner decided against it.

## Open questions

- How a change token is drawn when it passes a greyed station.

Spec impact: none; `.github/workflows/factory-video.yml` is protected, so the workflow change is a signed batch.

title: Run Kokoro as a separate program, as SPEC-002-R8 does for Piper
description:
## Context

`factory-video/narrate.py` imports `kokoro_onnx`, which loads phonemizer and espeak-ng. Decision 0008 read those as GPL-3.0 at medium confidence; that reading is not rechecked. SPEC-002-R8 already requires the walkthrough's Piper voice to run only as a separate program that no repository file imports. The owner chose the same rule for Kokoro on 2026-11-08 (decision 0008).

## Outcome

No file in the repository imports `kokoro_onnx`; the factory video's voice runs as a separate program from a hash-pinned venv under `build/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `git grep kokoro_onnx` finds no import in a repository file. Checked by a test.
- [ ] The narration's digests and lengths are unchanged, so `narrate.py check` passes without `narrate.py update`. Checked by the factory-video build.
- [ ] The licence reading is rechecked against each package's own licence file, with dates, in decision 0008.

Spec impact: none. `factory-video/narration/` is protected, so a change to its pins is a signed batch.

title: Amend SPEC-001-R3 so the allowlist check reads every requirements.in
description:
## Context

The allowlist check (SPEC-001-R3) reads only `package.json` files. `kokoro-onnx` is approved by a line in `allowed-deps.txt`, but nothing checks Python dependencies against that list, so an unlisted Python package passes. The owner chose on 2026-11-08 to make it a check (decision 0008).

## Outcome

A package named in any committed `requirements.in` and absent from `allowed-deps.txt` fails the allowlist check with its name as the identifier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SPEC-001-R3 amended, approver-signed. Checked by the signatures check.
- [ ] `node scripts/checks.ts allowlist` fails with `CHECK allowlist FAILED: <name>` for an unlisted name in a `requirements.in`. Checked by a test whose title names SPEC-001-R3.
- [ ] It passes on `main` with every current `requirements.in`. Checked by the candidate run.

## Out of scope

## Open questions

- Whether a scenario like B6 is needed for a Python name.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R3 (amend). `specs/` and `scripts/checks.ts` are protected, so a signed batch.

title: Keep the AWS account ID out of public Actions logs, then decide on old logs and history
description:
## Context

This repository is public. After `proposals/public-hygiene/` lands, no tracked file holds the sandbox AWS account ID, but it is still published in three places:

- Public Actions logs. Four workflows assume a role with `role-to-assume: ${{ vars.<NAME>_ROLE_ARN }}`: `pipeline.yml` (deploy), `issue-triage.yml`, `producer.yml` and `scenarios.yml`. GitHub prints a step's inputs before the step runs, and repository variables are never masked, so the full role ARN, account ID included, appears in clear. `main` run 42501305077 shows it in the `configure-aws-credentials` step; every later line shows `***` because that action masks the ID once it has credentials.
- Git history: 7 commits add or remove the ID.
- Earlier run logs, from every run that assumed a role.

Nothing in the code needs the number in the repository: `infra/sandbox` reads it from `data.aws_caller_identity`, and the deploy step from `aws sts get-caller-identity`. `aws-setup.sh` takes it as `SANDBOX_ACCOUNT_ID` and checks it against the profile. Public readers need only the shape, a sandbox member account with an SCP.

Owner decisions of 2026-11-08, in this order:
1. The owner keeps the ID only on their machine, in a shell profile or AWS config. No repository change.
2. Move the four role ARNs from repository variables to secrets, as a signed batch of its own. Secrets are masked from the first line.
3. and 4. Decide together whether to delete or expire the earlier run logs, and whether to rewrite history as D24 did. Without step 2, every new run would publish the ID again, so steps 3 and 4 alone would not hold.

## Outcome

No new run log and no tracked file shows the AWS account ID, and the owner has decided what happens to the earlier logs and the history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four workflows read each role ARN from `secrets.<NAME>_ROLE_ARN`, and no workflow references `vars.*_ROLE_ARN`. Checked by a test over `.github/workflows/` and by the workflows check.
- [ ] SPEC-001-R85 is amended so the producer's agent job may reference exactly one secret, its role ARN, and only in the `configure-aws-credentials` step, outside the agent's `env -i`. R86's sentence on `github.sh --vars` and `PRODUCER_ROLE_ARN` is amended to match. Both are approver-signed. Checked by the signatures check and by tests whose titles name R85 and R86.
- [ ] `scripts/bootstrap/github.sh` sets the four ARNs as secrets and deletes the four variables, and the owner runs it once, because only the owner may create secrets. Checked by `gh secret list` showing the four names and `gh variable list` showing no `*_ROLE_ARN`.
- [ ] The next `main` deploy's log shows `role-to-assume: ***`. Checked by reading that run's log.
- [ ] The owner's decision on earlier logs and history is recorded, with the date, in `docs/deviations.md` beside D24.

## Out of scope

- Treating the account ID as a credential: it grants nothing alone. This item is about not publishing it.
- Any IAM or trust-policy change.

## Open questions

- The current location and default of the repository's log-retention setting. Not verified on 2026-11-08.
- Whether to delete the earlier runs, about 120 pipeline runs plus triage, scenarios and producer runs, or let them expire.
- Whether a history rewrite is worth doing, given that anyone's earlier clone keeps the ID.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R85 and SPEC-001-R86 (amend). `.github/`, `scripts/bootstrap/` and `specs/` are protected, so a signed batch.

title: Share one test fixture for the scripts' temporary-repository tests
description:
## Context

The 2026-11-08 autonomous run staged eight batches (`docs/notes/autonomous-run-2026-11-08.md`). Once they land, they add 2,158 lines of code, configuration and tests to `main`, of which about 1,210 are tests. Measured on a simulated landing of all eight batches, about 160 lines sit in 4-line blocks repeated across files. Most of them are one pattern: five test files each build a temporary repository with a bare origin, write a stub `gh` and run a script against it:

| File | Builds its own |
|---|---|
| `test/land.test.ts` | `makeRepo`, `stubGh`, `git`, `originRef`, `events` |
| `test/land-delivery.test.ts` | `makeRepo`, `stubGh`, `git`, `originRef`, `events` |
| `test/land-presign.test.ts` (new) | `makeRepo`, `stubGh`, stub `node`, `npm`, `npx` |
| `test/producer-script.test.ts` (new) | `repo`, `stubGh` |
| `test/aws-setup.test.ts` | `makeRepo`, `stubGh`, and stubs for `aws`, `terraform` and others |

The owner asked on 2026-11-08 whether the run's code would be refactored. The agent recommended doing it after the batches land, not before: four of these files are inside staged batches whose copies build on each other, so a refactor before landing means restaging and re-reviewing up to six batches for 3 to 5% of the change. After landing, `test/` is not a protected path, so the refactor is one unsigned agent commit.

## Outcome

The five files share one fixture module, and each keeps only the stub behaviour its own script needs. No test is dropped or weakened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new `test/helpers/` module makes a temporary clone with a bare origin, writes executable stubs into a directory first on `PATH`, and runs a script with a given environment and standard input. Checked by reading it and by the five files importing it.
- [ ] The five files use it, and the number of tests and their titles are unchanged. Checked by `npx vitest list --json` before and after: the same titles.
- [ ] The five files shrink by at least 60 lines in total, net of the new module. Checked by `git diff --stat`.
- [ ] Every test passes in the candidate run, which has `ssh-keygen`, and the trace check passes. Checked by the candidate run.
- [ ] The commit carries `Spec:` trailers for the requirements the changed tests name: SPEC-001-R30, R41, R86, R210, R212, R213 and R217. Checked by the trace check.

## Out of scope

- The bash helpers `say`, `fail` and `ask`, repeated in three owner scripts. Sharing them needs `source`, which `land.sh`'s own test forbids so that it runs only reviewed code.
- `producer.sh`'s fallback for a `gh workflow run` that prints no URL: gh 2.89.0's help says it prints the URL only "if available".
- Staging batches as patches instead of full copies, which would shrink `proposals/` but is a signed change to `land.sh`.

## Open questions

- Whether `test/aws-setup.test.ts` should move to the shared module too, or keep its own harness: its stubs for `aws` and `terraform` are about 100 lines and specific to it. Recommendation: share only the clone and `PATH` parts.

Not done before landing: the batches were already preflighted and reviewed, and their copies depend on each other.

title: Encrypt the break-glass alarm topic with a key EventBridge can use
description:
## Context

The break-glass alarm (SPEC-001-R217) is an EventBridge rule that sends every assumption of break-glass, and every call by its IAM user, to an SNS topic with two email subscriptions. On 2026-11-09, after `proposals/break-glass-mfa/` landed, the owner made four boundary calls and received no email. CloudWatch showed, for 22:30 to 23:30 UTC, `TriggeredRules` 3 and `FailedInvocations` 3 for the rule: it matched, and every delivery failed. Both subscriptions are confirmed.

The topic is encrypted with the AWS managed key `alias/aws/sns` (`infra/sandbox/main.tf`). AWS's SNS developer guide, "Enable compatibility between event sources from AWS services and encrypted topics" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-key-management.html, read 2026-11-09), says such event sources need a customer managed key that grants the service principal, `events.amazonaws.com` for EventBridge, `kms:GenerateDataKey*` and `kms:Decrypt`. The AWS managed key's policy cannot be changed, so no alarm could ever be delivered. Lesson L2 records that break-glass had never been assumed before, so the gap went unseen.

The same page says AWS does not support `aws:SourceAccount`, `aws:SourceArn` or `aws:SourceOrgID` in that key-policy statement for EventBridge. The grant cannot be scoped to the rule.

If this is not done, any use of break-glass, or of its user's access key, goes unreported.

## Outcome

The topic is encrypted with a customer managed key used by nothing else. Its policy lets EventBridge use it and lets the deploy role read it. Each boundary call of the break-glass runbook (`docs/notes/break-glass-mfa.md`, step 7) sends an alarm email, and the rule's `FailedInvocations` stays 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test/break-glass.test.ts` fails if any topic uses `alias/aws/sns`, if the alarm topic does not use `aws_kms_key.break_glass_alarm`, if that key encrypts anything else, or if its policy statements differ from `Account`, `DeployReads` and `EventBridgePublishes`. Checked by the test check.
- [ ] `aws-setup.sh`'s `infra/sandbox` plan, run as the sandbox admin with the SCP attached, is 1 to add and 1 to change, and applies. Checked by the owner at the plan prompt.
- [ ] The next deploy from `main` plans no change. Checked in its log.
- [ ] After the apply, the four step-7 calls each produce an email, and the rule's `Invocations` is above 0 with `FailedInvocations` 0 for that hour. Checked by the owner with `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics`.

## Out of Scope

- Scoping the EventBridge grant: AWS does not support it for EventBridge-to-encrypted topics.
- Removing one of the two email subscriptions: optional owner cleanup, recorded in the notes.
- Changing the deploy role's IAM policy: only break-glass may, and the key policy grants the reads instead.

## Open Questions

- The rule matched 3 events in an hour with at least four matching calls. Whether a denied AssumeRole by another principal is matched, as SPEC-001-R217 requires, is checked by counting emails after the fix.

## Closed 2026-11-11

`proposals/alarm-key/` landed as the owner-signed `b9f6432`; `aws-setup.sh` applied the new key and the topic change on 2026-11-11 (1 added, 1 changed). Four boundary calls on 2026-11-10 produced emails for three: the break-glass user's refused `AssumeRole`, its refused `ListBuckets`, and the assumption with a code. The deploy of `d750b3e` planned no change. Criterion 4 is met for every call the rule matches; the fourth call, another identity's refused `AssumeRole`, is not matched, because CloudTrail records it with `requestParameters` `null`. That, and the session token the alarm email carries, moved to `who-gets-the-keys-r3m`. Outcome and corrections: `docs/notes/alarm-key.md`, "What happened".

title: Check the owner's machine before each step, and make land.sh and aws-setup.sh tell the truth
description:
## Context

From 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11 the owner stopped 13 times on something other than the change under review (`docs/notes/owner-queue-lessons-2026-11-10.md`, L23 to L30 and L32). The causes were on the owner's machine (Node 24.1.0 first on the PATH, `ykman` missing, two YubiKeys, SSO expired) or in the owner scripts: `land.sh` reported three runs as failed when only its watch had lost the connection, said "approve" for a batch whose Terraform the deploy role cannot apply, and gave no clear cue to touch the key; `aws-setup.sh` printed a command too long to copy and a sign-in hint for the wrong profile. Each stop cost a round of questions, and two put a deploy or an enrollment at risk. `scripts/bootstrap/` is a protected path, so this is a staged batch the owner signs.

## Outcome

One command, `scripts/bootstrap/doctor.sh`, tells the owner before a step whether the machine is ready, and how to fix each gap. The owner scripts report only real failures, say when not to approve, prompt for every touch, and end with a short block to paste to the agent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `doctor.sh` checks, each with its exact fix: Node in `package.json`'s `engines` range, else Homebrew's `node@<major>`; `gh` signed in; git 2.34 or later; an `ssh-keygen` with security-key support as git uses it; exactly one YubiKey plugged in, with OATH enabled; AWS credentials valid for the sandbox and management profiles, naming the SSO source profile when a role profile fails. Checked by tests with stub `node`, `gh`, `git`, `ykman` and `aws`.
- [ ] `land.sh` runs the doctor first, and uses `node@<major>` when the PATH's `node` is out of range. Checked by a test.
- [ ] After `gh run watch` exits nonzero, `land.sh` reads the run's status and conclusion, and reports a failure only on conclusion `failure`; otherwise it prints that it lost contact with run N, and the command to watch it again. Checked by a test with a stub `gh` that fails the watch on a passing run.
- [ ] A `LAND.txt` key such as `owner-apply: aws-setup.sh` makes `land.sh` print that step and "do not approve yet" instead of "approve". Checked by a test.
- [ ] `land.sh --lockfile <package>` updates only that package in `package-lock.json`, shows the diff, refuses if anything else changed, signs, pushes a candidate branch and finishes as `--to-main`. Checked by a test with stub `npm`.
- [ ] Every signature in the owner scripts is preceded by its own touch line, and on macOS a notification; `Couldn't sign message: invalid format?` is reported as "no touch in time, or the wrong key; nothing was committed". Checked by a test with a stub `ssh-keygen`.
- [ ] `aws-setup.sh` prints copy-safe `ykman` commands, and its sign-in hint names the SSO source profile. `land.sh` and `aws-setup.sh` end with a summary of 10 lines or fewer, with no account ID, copied to the clipboard on macOS. Checked by tests.

## Out of scope

- Turning off the YubiKey's OTP application: the owner's choice, not the scripts'.
- Retrying a lost network connection inside Terraform: the backend stops before any change, and a rerun is the fix.

## Open questions

- Whether the doctor should refuse, or only warn, when the approver key and the break-glass code are on one device.

## Closed 2026-11-12

Landed as `1d6aed9`, signed (SPEC-001-R218 to R225): `doctor.sh`, and `land.sh` and `aws-setup.sh` changes for each criterion. `main` run 43287714587 passed and its deploy planned no change. Two staged fixes landed first, unsigned, after the owner's macOS preflight showed what Linux could not: a Homebrew `node@24` found by the doctor in tests (`9283de9`), and BSD `seq 0` (`19db7bf`). The open question was answered on 2026-11-12: one YubiKey holding both keys gets a note, not a refusal. Notes: `docs/notes/owner-tooling.md`.

title: Add owner-step rules to CLAUDE.md, and keep the hooks off the agent's own read-only commands
description:
## Context

Four of the 13 stops of 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-11 came from the agent's own instructions (`docs/notes/owner-queue-lessons-2026-11-10.md`, L21 to L23 and L30): an expected Terraform plan that missed a data source read during the apply, a bash glob on the owner's zsh, a command too long to copy, and a signing step whose touch was mentioned in passing. L33 adds two hook frictions: the `no-sign` hook blocked a read-only search because its text named signing settings, and gitleaks blocked every command while a subagent's worktree sat under `.claude/worktrees/`. `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` are protected paths, so this is a staged batch the owner signs, after `who-gets-the-keys-k7d` so its rules can name that batch's `owner-apply` key.

## Outcome

`CLAUDE.md`'s "Owner steps" carries the rules below, and the agent's worktrees no longer trip the repository's hooks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Owner steps" says: before stating an expected Terraform plan, list each data source that depends on a changed resource; write commands for zsh; no command to copy longer than one screen line; a signing step's touch is its own line before the command; a batch the deploy role cannot apply declares `owner-apply` and its notes say "do not approve yet" first; before saying a check passed on `main`, account for checks that read data at run time, such as sca and sast. Checked by reading the staged `CLAUDE.proposed.md`.
- [ ] Agent worktrees are created outside the checkout, or `.claude/worktrees/` is excluded from the hook's gitleaks scan, whichever the owner chooses. Checked by a test of the hook.
- [ ] The `Purpose` line's count of bad changes matches `scenarios/scenarios.yaml` (22 since B81). Checked by reading it.

## Out of scope

- Loosening the `no-sign` hook's text match: it is a tripwire in front of the security key, and a false positive costs one rephrased read.

## Open questions

- Worktrees outside the checkout, or a gitleaks exclusion: the exclusion is simpler but widens what the scan skips.

title: Alarm on refused break-glass attempts by any identity, and send no credentials in the alarm email
description:
## Context

On 2026-11-10, after `who-gets-the-keys-q2n` fixed the alarm's delivery, four boundary calls emailed three times (`docs/notes/owner-queue-lessons-2026-11-10.md`, L31; `docs/notes/alarm-key.md`, "What happened"). The fourth, another identity's refused `AssumeRole` on break-glass, was not matched: CloudTrail records a refused `AssumeRole` with `requestParameters` `null`, so the rule's `roleArn` pattern cannot match it. Someone probing break-glass from another identity goes unreported. Second, the alarm email is the whole CloudTrail event, so for a successful assumption it carries the session's access key ID and session token, though not its secret key. Nothing checks delivery end to end, which is how the alarm went undelivered from its first day. The Terraform is in `infra/sandbox`, a protected path.

## Outcome

Every attempt to assume break-glass, refused or not and by any identity, emails `ALERT_EMAIL` a trimmed message with who, what, when, where from and the error, and no credentials. An on-demand check shows the alarm still delivers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The rule also matches `AssumeRole` events with an `errorCode` whose `errorMessage` names the break-glass role, using a pattern EventBridge documents (verify the wildcard or prefix syntax in AWS's EventBridge documentation first, and quote it in the notes). Checked by a test of the Terraform and by the owner repeating the four boundary calls: four emails.
- [ ] The target sends a trimmed message through an input transformer: principal, event name, time, source IP, error code and the role. Checked by a test, and by an email with no `responseElements`.
- [ ] An on-demand check reads the rule's `Invocations` and `FailedInvocations` with the read-only probe role and fails if any invocation failed in the window. Checked by running it.
- [ ] SPEC-001-R217 is amended to say "every attempt" and to name the trimmed message.

## Out of scope

- Alarming on every refused call by any identity: noise. Only break-glass attempts.

## Open questions

- Whether the deploy role may change the rule and its target, or the owner applies it with `aws-setup.sh` as for `who-gets-the-keys-q2n`.

title: Show what is built against the specs, in the README and the factory video, kept current by a check
description:
## Context

The owner asked on 2026-11-09 whether a visual shows how much is built against the target, updated with every change and shown in the README and the factory video. It does not. `factory-video/claims.json` grades 26 claims (on 2026-11-11: 12 built, 5 partly built, 6 planned, 1 open, 2 illustrative), but its report is an Actions artifact that expires after 30 days, and its statuses come from lists kept by hand: claim C04 cited `who-gets-the-keys-j5t` as open for two days after j5t landed. `docs/practices.md` is regenerated only by hand, and the README's counts are typed. The factory video shows the target by design, not progress.

## Outcome

The README shows a generated SVG with claims by status, practices by coverage and scenarios local or on demand, plus dynamic badges from a committed JSON, and a check fails when any of them is stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run progress` writes `docs/progress.json` and `docs/progress.svg` from `factory-video/claims.json`, `practices.yaml` and `scenarios/scenarios.yaml`. Checked by a test.
- [ ] The README shows the SVG and shields.io dynamic badges that read `docs/progress.json`, as the mutation-floor badge reads `stryker.config.json`. Checked by reading it.
- [ ] A check in `scripts/checks.ts` fails when the committed files differ from regenerated output, when a `planned` claim ID is defined in `specs/`, when an `open` backlog ID is closed, or when `docs/practices.md` is stale. Checked by tests, one per failure.
- [ ] The factory video still shows the whole target, and marks each claim on screen as built, partly built, planned or open, from the same status `npm run progress` computes, with an end card of the counts: built so far, and what is left. Checked by a test of the label data and by reading a still.
- [ ] The check is staged as a batch the owner signs; the generator and README are an agent commit. Checked by the landing.

## Out of scope

- A workflow that commits the visual: it needs `contents: write`, and `main` would move to a commit no check ran on (SPEC-001-R41).

## Open questions

- A requirement ID above the highest on every remote branch at staging time.

## Correction, 2026-11-12

An earlier version put progress inside the factory video out of scope ("the video shows the target by design"). The owner corrected that on 2026-11-12: the video keeps showing the full target, and also shows what is built and what is left. The criterion above replaces that exclusion.

## Closed 2026-11-12

Landed as `2a86484`, signed (SPEC-001-R226 to R229), after the unsigned `8dce7fe`: `npm run progress` writes `docs/progress.json` and `docs/progress.svg`, the README shows them with two badges, a test fails when either or `docs/practices.md` is stale, and the factory video ends on a silent card of what is built and what is left. `main` run 43297996811 passed, and the `factory-video` build of `8dce7fe` passed 37 of 37 checks. One difference from the criteria: the staleness check is a test in the test check, not a check in `scripts/checks.ts`, so it needed no change to the ordered checks. Notes: `docs/notes/progress.md`.
